title: Is breakfast the most important meal of the day?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: old-fashioned word for a very poor person
sudden increase in a value being measured
the chemical processes inside the human body, especially those which process food
deliberately miss something, or not do it
how your brain decides how much you should eat

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 您好，这里是BBC英语教学的6 Minute English。

sentences.en: I'm Georgie. And I'm Phil. Did you have any breakfast today, Georgie, or did you skip it?
sentences.zh: 我是Georgie。我是Phil。Georgie，你今天吃早饭了吗，还是不吃了？

sentences.en: I did have some breakfast. On the way to the office, I got myself a pastry and a coffee.
sentences.zh: 我吃了早饭。在去办公室的路上，我买了一个糕点和一杯咖啡。

sentences.en: What about you? I had a big bowl of porridge, but it was at six o'clock this morning so I'm hungry again now.
sentences.zh: 你呢？我吃了一大碗粥，但那是今天早上六点吃的，所以我现在又饿了。

sentences.en: And you might soon be hungry as well because we're going to talk about breakfast.
sentences.zh: 你可能很快也会饿，因为我们要聊聊早餐。

sentences.en: How important is it? Let's start by hearing from Professor Alexandra Johnstone, a nutrition scientist who spoke to Ruth Alexander, host of BBC World Service programme The Food Chain.
sentences.zh: 它有多重要？让我们先听听营养科学家Alexandra Johnstone的看法，她接受了BBC世界服务部节目The Food Chain的主持人Ruth Alexander的采访。

sentences.en: I am supporting the meme 'breakfast like a king and dine like a pauper '.
sentences.zh: 我支持“早餐吃得像国王，晚餐吃得像乞丐”这个观点。

sentences.en: For you then, breakfast is the most important meal of the day.
sentences.zh: 对你来说，早餐是一天中最重要的一餐。

sentences.en: I agree. So, it's really important, particularly for people who are trying to maintain a healthy weight and people who are trying to lose weight.
sentences.zh: 我同意。所以，它真的很重要，特别是对于那些试图保持健康体重和试图减肥的人。

sentences.en: Alexandra says that you should 'breakfast like a king and dine like a pauper '.
sentences.zh: Alexandra说你应该“早餐吃得像国王，晚餐吃得像乞丐”。

sentences.en: Pauper is an old-fashioned word for a very poor person.
sentences.zh: Pauper是一个过时的词，指非常穷的人。

sentences.en: The expression means have a big breakfast and a small dinner.
sentences.zh: 这个表达的意思是早餐吃得多，晚餐吃得少。

sentences.en: We're going to find out some of the reasons that Alexandra and other experts recommend doing this.
sentences.zh: 我们将找出一些原因，解释为什么Alexandra和其他专家建议这样做。

sentences.en: And as usual, we'll learn some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，我们会学到一些实用的新单词和短语。

sentences.en: And remember – you'll find all the vocabulary and a quiz on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 记住——你可以在我们的网站bbclearningenglish.com上找到所有的词汇和一个小测验。

sentences.en: OK. But first I have a question for you, Phil.
sentences.zh: 好的。但首先我有一个问题要问你，Phil。

sentences.en: According to a recent survey, which of the following is the most popular breakfast in the UK?
sentences.zh: 根据最近的一项调查，以下哪项是英国最受欢迎的早餐？

sentences.en: Is it: a) eggs, b) toast, or c) cereal? Well, I think people like to keep it simple so I'm going to say toast.
sentences.zh: 是：a) 鸡蛋，b) 吐司，还是 c) 麦片？嗯，我认为人们喜欢保持简单，所以我选吐司。

sentences.en: OK. Well, we'll find out the answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的。嗯，我们会在节目后面揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Let's hear some reasons for why we should breakfast like a king or queen.
sentences.zh: 让我们听听为什么我们应该像国王或女王一样吃早餐的一些原因。

sentences.en: Courtney Peterson, who researches eating behaviours, explains how the time of day affects how our bodies process food, on BBC World Service programme The Food Chain: And so, if you can eat a large breakfast in the morning, and/or I would even say a large lunch in the morning, your body's going to be better at metabolising that food.
sentences.zh: 研究饮食行为的Courtney Peterson在BBC世界服务部节目The Food Chain中解释了一天中的时间如何影响我们的身体处理食物：“所以，如果你能在早上吃一顿丰盛的早餐，或者甚至可以说在早上吃一顿丰盛的午餐，你的身体会更好地代谢这些食物。”

sentences.en: And what that means is your body's going to actually… your blood sugar levels won't spike as high, you might burn slightly more fat, you might burn slightly more calories from eating earlier in the day.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你的身体实际上……你的血糖水平不会飙升得那么高，你可能会燃烧稍微多一点的脂肪，在一天中较早的时候进食可能会让你燃烧稍微多一点的热量。

sentences.en: Whereas if you had… if you eat most of your food later in the day, your metabolism is actually slower later in the day.
sentences.zh: 而如果你有……如果你在一天中较晚的时候吃大部分食物，你的新陈代谢在一天中较晚的时候其实是较慢的。

sentences.en: So, for instance, if you ate the same, I don't know, bowl of ice cream in the morning, the afternoon and the evening, your blood sugar levels will spike significantly higher in the afternoon and the evening.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，如果你在早晨、下午和晚上吃同样的一碗冰淇淋，你的血糖水平在下午和晚上会显著飙升得更高。

sentences.en: We heard the noun metabolism. This is a word that refers to the chemical processes in your body, and we most often use it to talk about those that convert food into energy.
sentences.zh: 我们听到了名词metabolism（新陈代谢）。这个词指的是你身体里的化学过程，我们最常用来谈论那些把食物转化为能量的过程。

sentences.en: And we also heard had the verb form – metabolise.
sentences.zh: 我们还听到了动词形式——metabolise（代谢）。

sentences.en: Courtney talked about blood sugar levels spiking.
sentences.zh: Courtney谈到了血糖水平spiking（飙升）。

sentences.en: A spike is a sharp, pointed shape. If you see it on a line graph, it means that something has increased very rapidly.
sentences.zh: Spike是一个尖锐的点状形状。如果你在线形图上看到它，意味着某事增长得非常迅速。

sentences.en: We often use the noun spike to mean a sudden increase in a value that is being measured.
sentences.zh: 我们经常用名词spike来表示正在被测量的数值突然增加。

sentences.en: The verb spike means to suddenly increase.
sentences.zh: 动词spike的意思是突然增加。

sentences.en: We've heard that eating earlier in the day can be healthier for us.
sentences.zh: 我们已经听说在一天中较早的时候进食对我们的健康更有益。

sentences.en: Now, people often don't eat breakfast, sometimes because they don't have time and sometimes because they are trying to save money.
sentences.zh: 现在，人们经常不吃早餐，有时是因为他们没有时间，有时是因为他们想省钱。

sentences.en: Let's hear again from Professor Alexandra Johnstone, talking to BBC World Service's The Food Chain.
sentences.zh: 让我们再次聆听Alexandra Johnstone教授接受BBC世界服务部The Food Chain采访的谈话。

sentences.en: Now, breakfast skipping is interesting because my own work would tend to suggest – and that sort of observational, large-scale, epidemiological studies would also support this – that people who have a regular breakfast are actually leaner.
sentences.zh: 现在，不吃早餐很有趣，因为我自己的研究倾向于表明——这种观察性的、大规模的流行病学研究也将支持这一点——经常吃早餐的人实际上更瘦。

sentences.en: And my own work would tend to suggest that having your largest meal of the day in the morning period gives you a much better appetite control, which then means it's much easier to control food intake later in the day.
sentences.zh: 我自己的研究倾向于表明，在早晨吃一天中最大的一餐能给你提供好得多的食欲控制，这反过来意味着更容易控制晚些时候的食物摄入量。

sentences.en: Alexandra starts by mentioning 'breakfast skipping '.
sentences.zh: Alexandra首先提到了“breakfast skipping（跳过早餐）”。

sentences.en: If you skip something, then you don't do it.
sentences.zh: 如果你skip某事，那么你就不做这件事。

sentences.en: Bad students might skip lessons – they don't go to them.
sentences.zh: 坏学生可能会skip课——他们不去上课。

sentences.en: If you skip a meal, it means that you don't eat it.
sentences.zh: 如果你skip一顿饭，意思就是你没吃它。

sentences.en: We also heard that people who have a regular breakfast are leaner.
sentences.zh: 我们还听到经常吃早餐的人更瘦。

sentences.en: If someone is lean, then they're not fat.
sentences.zh: 如果一个人是lean的，那么他们就不胖。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons given why people might be leaner is that they have better appetite control.
sentences.zh: 人们更瘦的原因之一是他们有更好的食欲控制。

sentences.en: Appetite control is where your brain decides how much you should eat.
sentences.zh: Appetite control是指你的大脑决定你应该吃多少。

sentences.en: Thanks, Georgie. Now, I think it's time that we heard the answer to your question.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，Georgie。现在，我想是时候听听你那个问题的答案了。

sentences.en: Yes, it is. OK. I asked, "According to a recent survey, what is the most popular breakfast in the UK?"
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。好的。我问过：“根据最近的一项调查，英国最受欢迎的早餐是什么？”

sentences.en: And I said, "Toast." …which was the most popular in London, but the most popular in the country as a whole was cereal, and that's according to a survey by a cereal manufacturer.
sentences.zh: 我说过：“吐司。”……这是伦敦最受欢迎的，但全国范围内最受欢迎的是麦片，根据一家麦片制造商的调查。

sentences.en: So, I'm afraid you got it wrong. OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with pauper, which is an old-fashioned word for a very poor person.
sentences.zh: 所以，恐怕你猜错了。好的。让我们回顾一下我们学过的词汇，从pauper开始，这是一个过时的词，指非常穷的人。

sentences.en: When we're talking about data, it spikes when it increases suddenly.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论数据时，当它突然增加时，它就会spike。

sentences.en: Metabolism refers to the chemical processes inside your body, especially those which process food.
sentences.zh: Metabolism指的是你体内的化学过程，尤其是那些处理食物的过程。

sentences.en: If you skip something, you miss it; you don't do it.
sentences.zh: 如果你skip某事，你就会错过它；你没有做它。

sentences.en: If someone is lean, then they are not fat.
sentences.zh: 如果一个人是lean的，那么他们就不胖。

sentences.en: And finally, appetite control is how your brain decides how much you should eat.
sentences.zh: 最后，appetite control是你的大脑决定你应该吃多少的方式。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but why not head over to our website, bbclearningenglish.com, to try the quiz and worksheet for this episode?
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟又到了，但是为什么不去我们的网站bbclearningenglish.com做一下这期节目的小测验和练习题呢？

sentences.en: See you again soon. Goodbye! Bye!
sentences.zh: 很快再见。再见！再见！
